newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African defence minister seeks bigger budget.
newsitem.headline: South African defence minister seeks bigger budget.

text.p: Defence Minister Joe Modise said on Thursday cuts in South African military spending meant the country could not meet its defence needs.

"Our budget has been cut by 59 percent since 1989 in real terms. This is creating great difficulties," he said in a speech to parliament on the 1997/98 defence budget of 9.58 billion rand ($2.0 billion).
"The fact is, we are unable to sustain an adequate defence programme," Modise said. "Our police support and regional roles will be adversely affected."
He said there was no provision for new weapons like ships or aircraft.

"Important projects, like the Rooivalk, may fall through," Modise said, referring to a South African-developed combat helicopter which the country hopes to sell abroad. The future of the project depends heavily on a mooted sale to the South African Air Force.

Deputy Defence Minister Ronnie Kasrils said on Wednesday that Modise was involved in "intense" negotiations with Finance Minister Trevor Manuel in a bid to get an increase in the defence allocation, but so far Manuel had refused to budge.
Kasrils said Modise had asked Deputy President Thabo Mbeki to intercede and negotiations were continuing.
Manuel is committed to trimming the budget deficit as part of a macro-economic plan aimed at luring foreign investment and boosting growth.
Kasrils said there was no provision for South Africa to buy the four Corvettes which Modise wants for the navy.
But he said money for this could be made available if parliament and the cabinet approved a comprehensive review of defence needs completed this month.
Modise, in his speech on Thursday, referred to the navy's role in providing a ship for Zairean peace talks earlier this month.
"The navy patrols our coastline to deter poaching and smuggling... We provide a great deal of support for the police, in dealing with crime," he said.
"We can do all this as long as we get the funding. But the continuing reductions in our budget are seriously affecting our capacity to assist in these ways," Modise said.
He said "dramatic events" in the region showed the importance of a strong defence force in maintaining stability.
